exposure: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) use in the third trimester
outcome: Neonatal clinical signs possibly related to drug toxicity
cohort: Thirty-four pregnant women who were given SSRIs in the third trimester, referred to a hospital from January 2011 to July 2015, and their related children.
finding: Nineteen newborns presented clinical signs possibly related to drug toxicity, and a high umbilical/maternal plasma ratio of SSRI was observed in 10 of 15 evaluated newborns, suggesting individualized psychopharmacologic treatment based on maternal exposure and genetic background could minimize risks.
cross-section timing: At delivery and early neonatal period
